=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/assemble_agents.py: apply_block, registry section branch (the bottom-up insertion sequence after `if block.heading != REGISTRY_SECTION`, around the `if bullets:` / `if names:` blocks) | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When the `Stable log prefixes (contractual)` section has no existing bullets (either truly empty, or has only existing names), a fragment that adds both bullets and names — or only bullets — ends up with the `LOG_PREFIX.name=` lines appearing above the new `- PREFIX` bullets, which inverts the "bullets first, then names" ordering the contract documents.
  WHY: Insertion order is bottom-up: `other` → `names` → `bullets`. With no existing names, `_last_matching(lines, start, end, REGISTRY_NAME, continuation=False)` returns None, so names fall through to `_append_to_section` and land at the end of the section. When bullets are then processed, `first_name` is the just-inserted names line and `_last_matching(lines, start, first_name, REGISTRY_BULLET, continuation=True)` still returns None, so bullets also fall through to `_append_to_section` and land at the end. The fallback for bullets is "end of section" rather than "before the first name", so the final order is `LOG_PREFIX.name=…` followed by `- PREFIX`, which is backwards. This was identified by minimax in the prior pass and the autofix did not address it. The existing `test_log_prefixes_extend_both_registries` only exercises a non-empty registry, so the regression is uncovered. It primarily affects the consumer-repo use case the PR enables: a fresh `AGENTS.md` whose registry is empty would be assembled with the two registries in the wrong order.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "with a shared reader so nothing is missed in between" (PR description "Why" section)
  Expected change site: Static-context readers in `.github/workflows/orchestrate.yml`, `.github/workflows/orchestrate_clarify_respond.yml`, `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`, and `scripts/validate_process.sh`.
  Evidence of absence: The PR introduces `assemble_agents.py render` as the shared reader and wires it into `scripts/build_static_context.sh`, `tests/agents_doc.py`, and `tests/inventory_parity.py`. The other four readers still inline a direct `cat agents.md` (or `AGENTS.md` / `agents_canonical.md` consumer branch) in their own static-context assembly, so the model contexts they emit omit pending fragments until the release fold or consumer sync. The PR's own editor summary explicitly defers this as `TASK_GAP_DEFERRED` ("the PR only claims `build_static_context.sh` renders pending fragments"), but the "nothing is missed in between" framing in the description implies broader coverage than the implementation delivers.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

  PROBLEM: When the `Stable log prefixes (contractual)` section has no existing `- \`PREFIX\`` bullets and a fragment adds both bullets and `LOG_PREFIX.name=` lines, the assembled file places `LOG_PREFIX.name=` lines before the `- \`PREFIX\`` bullets. At line 303-306, names are inserted first via `_append_to_section` at the content end. Then at line 309-316, bullets are processed: `first_name` now points to the just-inserted name line, `_last_matching(REGISTRY_BULLET, start, first_name)` finds no bullets before it, so `at is None`, and `_append_to_section(lines, start, end, bullets)` places bullets at the content end — after the names. The established pattern in `agents.md` is bullets before names (the test `test_log_prefixes_extend_both_registries` only covers the non-empty case where both already exist).
  WHY: A fragment targeting an empty registry section (or a consumer `AGENTS.md` that has the section heading but no entries yet) produces a malformed agents file where `LOG_PREFIX.name=` lines precede their `- \`PREFIX\`` bullet descriptions, breaking the documented registry contract that bullets and names stay in parallel order.
